claims.hypothesis: The IRS3B disk is gravitationally unstable and IRS3B-c formed by disk fragmentation.
claims.experiment: Measure continuum surface density, fit central mass from disk kinematics, and calculate radial Toomre Q.
claims.result: IRS3B has Q < 1 beyond ∼120 au; the tertiary lies within a spiral arm.
claims.finding: The observations support in-situ fragmentation of a gravitationally unstable disk.

evidence.quote: We find the circum-multiple disk of IRS3B is gravitationally unstable (Q $<$ 1) for radii $>$ 120 au.
This coincides with the location of the spiral arms and the tertiary companion IRS3B-c, supporting the hypothesis that IRS3B-c was formed in situ via fragmentation of a gravitationally unstable disk.

claims.hypothesis: The disks trace Keplerian rotation suitable for measuring central masses.
claims.experiment: Compare PV rotation curves with radiative-transfer visibility fits.
claims.result: IRS3B: PV 1.15 M⊙ and pdspy 1.19 M⊙; IRS3A: PV 1.4 M⊙ and pdspy 1.51 M⊙.
claims.finding: Kinematic model masses agree with PV estimates.

evidence.quote: The *pdspy*modeling of IRS3B finds a mass of $1.19^{+0.13}_{-0.07}$ M$_{\odot}$, comparable to the PV diagram fit of 1.15$^{+0.09}_{-0.09}$ M$_{\odot}$.
The *pdspy*modeling fit for IRS3A yields mass $1.51^{+0.06}_{-0.07}$ M$_{\odot}$which is also comparable to the PV diagram estimate of 1.4 M$_{\odot}$.

claims.hypothesis: IRS3B-c measurably perturbs the surrounding disk kinematics.
claims.experiment: Search its local C17O PV diagram for velocities above the main disk profile.
claims.result: No excess detected; protostar mass <0.2 M⊙.
claims.finding: The tertiary has low mass and no detected excess kinematic signature.

evidence.quote: The velocity profile at IRS3B-c shows no evidence of any excess beyond the Keplerian profile from the main disk, indicating that it has very low mass.
Based on the non-detection, we can place upper limits on the mass of IRS3B-c source of $<$0.2 M$_{\odot}$

claims.hypothesis: Possible IRS3A spiral substructure is driven by gravitational instability.
claims.experiment: Calculate its Toomre Q profile from continuum surface density and central mass.
claims.finding: IRS3A is gravitationally stable under the adopted assumptions; substructure may have another origin.

evidence.quote: We find the protostellar disk of IRS3A is gravitationally stable (Q $>$5) for the entire disk.
Thus substructures in IRS3A may not be gravitationally driven spiral arms and could reflect other substructure.

claims.hypothesis: The wider IRS3A/B system formed through turbulent fragmentation.
claims.experiment: Compare disk/outflow orientations and systemic velocities.
claims.result: Nearly orthogonal disks and different system velocities.
claims.finding: Turbulent core fragmentation is the likely origin of the wider system.

evidence.quote: The larger IRS3A/B system (including the even wider companion L1448 NW) likely formed via turbulent fragmentation of the core during the early core collapse
as evidenced by the nearly orthogonal disk orientation and different system velocity for IRS3A and IRS3B.

claims.hypothesis: The inferred present accretion rates can build the observed masses during the Class 0 stage.
claims.experiment: Estimate accretion from luminosities, kinematic masses, and birth-line models.
claims.result: Inferred rates are insufficient over ∼160 kyr.
claims.finding: Periods of higher accretion are required.

evidence.quote: These accretion rates are unable to build up the observed protostellar masses within the typical lifetime of the Class 0 stage ($\sim$160 kyr)
thus require periods of higher accretion events to explain the observed protostellar masses.

referee_caveats_inferred: The supplied text loses coefficients in molecular abundances and several fitted quantities; exact radiative-transfer reproduction is blocked.
IRS3B instability begins at ∼120 au in the body and summary, versus ∼200 au in the abstract.
IRS3A accretion is 4.95×10−7 M⊙ yr−1 in the narrative and 5.43×10−7 in Table 6; retain both as distinct reported values.
The stated 300 pc luminosity context and 288 pc table scaling require reconciliation before recalculating temperatures and accretion.
Toomre Q depends on assumed temperature, opacity, gas-to-dust ratio, and azimuthal averaging of spiral structure.
PV and radiative-transfer mass agreement does not independently test Keplerian rotation, which is assumed in both mass models.
The tertiary upper limit has no stated confidence level or injection/recovery sensitivity test.
Text and tables give differing continuum sizes, position angles, and systemic velocities; exact answer keys must identify the measurement method.
